The file history dates this digital drawing to 29 April 2018. The page states the drawing is released under CC0 1.0; it is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph.

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry reports that both 机 and 機 occur in Shuowen as separate graphs: 机 is glossed 木也 and analyzed 从木几聲; 機 is glossed 主發謂之機 and analyzed 从木幾聲. It records distinct historical fanqie readings (居履 for 机; 居依 for 機), says later writers often borrowed 机 for 機 because of their similar sound, and reports that this established use became mainland China’s simplified form. This supports a substitution/borrowing relationship, not an ancestor-descendant claim. It gives Mandarin scopes including 机 readings jī and jǐ; the entry does not on this page establish the sound of the historic tree name independently.

search_audit.outcome: Search performed. Inspected the Academia Sinica database introduction and MOE dictionary entry; no exact Xiaoxuetang 机 or 機 record was retrieved in this run.

Search performed and Commons file page inspected. Its image is an identified modern Shuowen seal-style redraw with stated CC0 rights; direct SVG opening by the web tool failed because it does not accept SVG content, but the page supplies a direct image URL.

gaps: The inspected sources here do not independently establish oracle-bone or bronze forms or a graphic corruption sequence for 机/機. The chosen illustration is explicitly a modern redraw of a seal-script form, not a photograph or facsimile of an ancient artifact.

The old name and pronunciation of the tree sense associated with 机 are not independently recovered. A reconstruction of the character reading cannot by itself prove that tree-name pronunciation, so this research does not establish the sound basis for any proposed whole-graph loan from the tree word.

This run did not independently inspect earliest semantic attestations or the sequence of semantic extensions; the prior dossier’s account of received-text examples and its manuscript-date caveat remains the relevant limitation.
